strategies.overview: Paldean Tauros-F carves a strong niche in NU thanks to its solid matchup against staples like Alolan Ninetales, Amoonguss, and Incineroar. Paldean Tauros-F poses as a wallbreaker with strong STAB attacks that are hard to switch around. It can also use Bulk Up to increase its power and bulk, making it harder to revenge kill with physical attackers. Its Speed tier gives it an edge over common wallbreakers such as Porygon-Z, Toxtricity, and Chandelure, letting it revenge kill them if needed. Not only is it an offensive threat, it has great defensive merits, too. Its Fire typing gives it a useful immunity to Will-O-Wisp from Incineroar, Houndstone, and opposing Paldean Tauros-F; meanwhile, Intimidate gives it more opportunities to switch in against physical wallbreakers like Toxicroak, Decidueye, and Breloom. On the flip side, Paldean Tauros-F has poor Special Defense, which, when paired with its typing, lets it be easily revenge killed by faster Pokemon like Munkidori, Kilowattrel, and Inteleon, all of which can force it to Terastallize. Paldean Tauros-F is heavily threatened by bulky Water-types like Vaporeon, Milotic, and Gastrodon, all of which can use Tera Poison or Tera Fairy to tank Close Combat. It also faces competition with Paldean Tauros-W, which has a better typing while being easier to fit on teams. Wallbreakers like Chandelure and Basculegion-M as well as walls like Altaria are able to take advantage of Paldean Tauros-F's STAB attacks easily, giving them free turns to set up or use Defog, respectively.
strategies.comments:
Other Options

Cud Chew can be used alongside a Lum Berry to let Paldean Tauros-F set up in front of status users like Klefki and Amoonguss, but this is often unreliable and heavily relies on the matchup. Iron Head can be used to target Fairy-types like Diancie, Sylveon, and Scream Tail, though it isn't too efficient, as Earthquake hits Diancie already and the last two aren't common. Bulk Up sets can run Substitute; however, it has no way of dealing damage to Chandelure unless it wants to give up one of its STAB attacks.

Checks and Counters

Flying-types: Flying-types such as Scyther, Kilowattrel, Oricorio-P, and Oricorio-F threaten Paldean Tauros-F with their STAB moves, and the last two can often use it as an opportunity to set up. The first three don't enjoy switching into its Fire-type attacks, however, and Oricorio-F is OHKOed by Stone Edge. Altaria resists both of Paldean Tauros-F's STAB attacks and is only hit hard by Stone Edge while threatening it back with Brave Bird. Gligar resists Close Combat and doesn't take much damage from Paldean Tauros-F's Fire-type attacks; while it does hit it hard with Earthquake, it does not want to be hit by Will-O-Wisp.

Water-types: Paldean Tauros-F is heavily checked by defensive Water-types like Vaporeon, Milotic, and Gastrodon; the only one that it threatens to 2HKO is specially defensive Gastrodon. All of them can tank any damage from Paldean Tauros-F, heal it off, and hit it back with their STAB moves. Inteleon outspeeds Paldean Tauros-F and can OHKO it, while Basculegion-M resists both of its STAB attacks and use it as an opportunity to set up Substitute. Paldean Tauros-W can freely set up on Choice item variants of Paldean Tauros-F, while it and Basculegion-M can KO Paldean Tauros-F with Aqua Jet after Paldean Tauros-F has been weakened.

Ghost-types: Hisuian Typhlosion and Basculegion-M are both immune to Close Combat and resist Paldean Tauros-F's Fire-type STAB attacks, while Chandelure is immune to both of its STAB attacks, only being hit by Earthquake and Stone Edge.

movesets.name: Bulk Up
movesets.description:
Set Details

Raging Bull is a strong Fire-type STAB move that doesn't have recoil damage and can break Aurora Veil from Alolan Ninetales, but due to its lower Base Power compared to Flare Blitz, it misses out on OHKOing Pokemon like Toxicroak, Klefki, and offensive Alolan Ninetales. Trailblaze gives Paldean Tauros-F the opportunity to outspeed faster threats like Inteleon, Kilowatrel, and Scyther. Earthquake lets Paldean Tauros-F deal with Poison-type foes like Alolan Muk and Overqwil as well as one of its best checks in Chandelure. Will-O-Wisp can be used to weaken Pokemon like Toxicroak, Basculegion-M, and Copperajah so that Paldean-Tauros-F can set up on them for free, but Will-O-Wisp gets rid of its only way of dealing damage to Chandelure. Leftovers recuperates any health lost from Flare Blitz's recoil and gives Paldean Tauros-F some longevity, while Heavy-Duty Boots enables it to repeatedly switch in without worrying about entry hazards. Tera Grass turns its Ground- and Water-type weaknesses into resistances while simultaneously boosting Trailblaze's power, giving it the chance to OHKO Gastrodon and 2HKO Swampert. Tera Electric is useful for its defensive merits such as the resistances to Kilowattrel's STAB attacks as well as Air Slash from Oricorio-P and Oricorio-F; it also gives Paldean Tauros-F an immunity to Klefki's Thunder Wave. Tera Steel gives Paldean Tauros-F a favorable matchup against Munkidori while also letting it resist Flying-type moves from the aforementioned Kilowattrel and Oricorio formes.

Paldean Tauros-F enjoys being put on hyper offense and balance teams that take advantage of both its offensive prowess and defensive utility. It excels at threatening Steel- and Dark-types like Copperajah, Bronzong, and Incineroar, giving Psychic-type teammates like Munkidori, Uxie, and Galarian Articuno room to wallbreak or set up; all of these can pivot to Paldean Tauros-F with U-turn. In return, these aforementioned Pokemon threaten Poison-types that Paldean Tauros-F struggles with, like Galarian Slowbro, Tentacruel, and Tera Poison Vaporeon. Paldean Tauros-F also struggles with physically defensive Flying-types like Gligar, Altaria, and Galarian Articuno, which lets it pair well with Ice Beam users such as Porygon2, Vaporeon, and Milotic, as well as Diancie. Vaporeon's Wish heavily benefits Paldean Tauros-F, alleviating damage from Flare Blitz recoil and entry hazards. Bulky Dark- and Normal-types like Incineroar, Alolan Muk, Porygon2, and Dudunsparce pressure Ghost-types like Chandelure, Hisuian Typhlosion, and special attacking Basculegion-M. Dudunsparce and Porygon2 along with Klefki and Amoonguss can inflict paralysis on faster Pokemon like Munkidori, Inteleon, and Choice Scarf Porygon-Z and Paldean Tauros-W, letting Paldean Tauros-F outspeed them and not worry about needing to use Trailblaze. Paldean Tauros-F also enjoys Alolan Ninetales's Aurora Veil on hyper offense teams to make it harder to be revenge killed.

movesets.name: Choice Item
movesets.description:
Set Details

Choice Band turns Paldean Tauros-F into a dangerous wallbreaker, giving it the opportunity to 2HKO checks like Vaporeon, Milotic, and Galarian Slowbro. On the other hand, Choice Scarf enables it as a fast revenge killer, outspeeding the likes of Inteleon, Kilowattrel, and Flygon. Raging Bull should only be considered on Choice Band variants due to the extra power given by the item, as Choice Scarf sets need the extra power from Flare Blitz. Earthquake aims to take down Chandelure and Hisuian Typhlosion, which resist or are immune to both of Paldean Tauros-F's STAB attacks, as well as Poison-types like Alolan Muk, Overqwil, and Tera Poison Gastrodon. Stone Edge gives Paldean Tauros-F an edge over Flying-types like Scyther, Altaria, and Galarian Articuno. Wild Charge targets the aforementioned Flying-types as well as Water-types like Vaporeon and Milotic. Tera Fighting boosts the power of Close Combat, making it harder to switch into Paldean Tauros-F. Other Tera types like Electric and Steel can be used for their defensive traits like resisting Flying-type moves as well as Psychic-type moves for the latter.

These sets fit best on balance and offensive teams that require a strong wallbreaker to beat Steel-types. Diancie, Munkidori, and Cinccino all appreciate Paldean Tauros-F's ability to threaten Steel-types like Bronzong, Copperajah, and Klefki. Choice Scarf Paldean Tauros-F enjoys Spikes from users like Diancie, Gastrodon, and Gligar to apply more pressure on checks like Vaporeon, Gastrodon, and Tera Water Amoonguss. Choice Band variants enjoy the presence of Choice Scarf users like Flygon, Munkidori, and Porygon-Z to take down faster foes like Munkidori, Scream Tail, and Choice Scarf Chandelure. Kilowattrel pairs especially well with Paldean Tauros-F thanks to its solid matchup against Water- and Flying-types like Vaporeon, Paldean Tauros-W, and Scyther; in return, Paldean Tauros-F can take down Gastrodon, Incineroar, and Bronzong. Wish passers like Vaporeon and Sylveon work well alongside Paldean Tauros-F to alleviate any residual damage from entry hazards and recoil from Flare Blitz. Water-types tend to be a thorn in Paldean Tauros-F's side, so Pokemon like Flygon and Scyther that can weaken them over a battle fit well alongside it. Paldean Tauros-F appreciates the presence of a Steel-type to pivot into its checks, whether it's Bronzong for handling Munkidori and Flygon, Copperajah helping with Kilowattrel and Galarian Articuno, or Klefki laying Spikes and switching into Scyther and Galarian Slowbro. Dark-types like Incineroar and Alolan Muk help beat down Chandelure and Hisuian Typhlosion, while Wo-Chien targets Basculegion-M. Grassy Terrain teams enjoy the utility of Paldean Tauros-F, using it as a safe pivot to weaken Pokemon like Incineroar and Flygon that threaten Oricorio-P and Grafaiai. Paldean Tauros-F appreciates Avalugg, Scyther, and Altaria to remove any hazards so that it can switch in more. Future Sight users like Galarian Articuno love partnering with Paldean Tauros-F because it threatens any potential switch-ins to Future Sight like Bronzong, Copperajah, Incineroar, and Alolan Muk.

movesets.name: FIREFIGHTER (Defensive)
movesets.description:
• Will-O-Wisp and Intimidate make Paldean Tauros-F a potent check to physical attackers, notably enabling it reliably check Chien-Pao and Kingambit.

  • Raging Bull: This provides a powerful STAB attack that can also break screens, allowing Paldean Tauros-F’s teammates to clean up more easily.

  • Body Press Body Press is valuable because unlike Close Combat, it doesn’t cause defense drops.

  • Rock Tomb: Rock Tomb allows Paldean Tauros-F to check Volcarona despite its meager Special Defense.

  • Bulk Up: While this set is unlikely to sweep, Bulk Up does give Paldean Tauros-F a good way to punish foes that attempt to sacrifice their Pokemon to it.

  • Tera Dependency - Very Situational: Paldean Tauros-F should generally avoid Terastallizing, as its typing is a big part of what lets it act as such a sturdy check to Kingambit and other massive threats, such as Baxcalibur.

Items

  • Sitrus Berry / Figy Berry: A quick burst of recovery from a berry fits playing this set a bit more recklessly.

  • Heavy-Duty Boots: This allows Paldean Tauros-F to switch around more freely in after entry hazards are set.

  • Rocky Helmet: Paldean Tauros-F tends to force a lot of switches, so Rocky Helmet lets it get some useful chip damage when switching into moves like Chien-Pao's Crunch.

  • Leftovers: Leftovers is a high value item that other Pokemon want, but the gradual recovery is useful.

movesets.name: Offensive Screen Smasher
movesets.description:
• Paldean Tauros-F is fast enough to outspeed key threats such as Mimikyu and Modest Chi-Yu, making an offensive set viable.

  • Raging Bull versus Flare Blitz: Raging Bull might not be as powerful as Flare Blitz, but its ability to break Reflect and Light Screen give Paldean Tauros-F a unique niche.

  • Flame Charge versus Trailblaze: Flame Charge gives Paldean Tauros-F an unexpected late-game win condition, letting it outspeed threats such as Chien-Pao and Iron Bundle. Trailblaze is often weaker, but the greater chip dagainst against Water-types such as Azumarill can be beneficial.

  • Rock Tomb: Rock Tomb's speed control is useful when sacrificing Paldean Tauros-F against a threat and prevents Dragonite from getting easy Speed boosts.

  • Will-O-Wisp: Despite this set's offensive nature, Will-O-Wisp is good for punishing Dragonite, Dragapult, and slower foes that may Terrastallize, such as Ting-Lu and Kingambit.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: Paldean Tauros-F makes major use of its unique typing defensively, so it only needs to Terastallize for situational win conditions.

  • Grass: A Grass Tera type makes Paldean Tauros-F far less vulnerable to Rotom-W and Rotom-W, in addition to dealing with Focus Sash Breloom.

  • Fairy: When paired with Tera Blast, a Fairy Tera type means Dragonite will no longer wall Paldean Tauros-F without Teratsallizing itself.

Items

  • Eject Pack: With Close Combat, this will give Paldean Tauros-F a powerful, one-time use pivot option.

  • Life Orb: This high value item can be tough to slot in, but the increased power makes sweeping with a Speed boost much easier.

  • Mirror Herb: Mirror Herb punishes setup sweepers even more effectively and pairs especially well with Intimidate.

movesets.name: Assault Vest
movesets.description:
• With an Assault Vest, Paldean Tauros-F finds itself a niche checking Choice Band Chien-Pao, Flutter Mane, and Iron Moth.

  • Raging Bull Despite Flare Blitz having more power, Raging Bull is Paldean Tauros-F's preferred STAB move as a result of its ability to break Aurora Veil, Reflect, and Light Screen, as well as the lack of recoil associated with the move.

  • Iron Head vs Stone Edge Iron Head is used because of its ability to hit foes that can Terastallize into Fairy-types, such as Dondozo and some Dragonite; it also provides a midground against Rock-types such as Garganacl and Tyranittar. It also is Paldean Tauros-F's best shot at OHKOing Flutter Mane without Terastallizing. However, Stone Edge can be used in lieu of it, as it is Tauros-F's best chance of defeating Iron Moth.

Tera Types

  • Steel: Terastallizing into a Steel-type allows Paldean Tauros-F to be immune to Acid Spray attempts from Iron Moth, as well as boosting the power of Iron Head. It also allows Paldean Tauros-B to defeat Flutter Mane more easily, as Flutter Mane would otherwise need lots of defensive investment to survive it.

  • Grass: Tera Grass prevents Azumarill's Liquidation from OHKOing Paldean Tauros-F, as well as providing a boost to Trailblaze.

  • Fire: Like Tera Steel, Tera Fire provides useful resistance to Fairy, notably Flutter Mane. It also allows Paldean Tauros-B to OHKO Flutter Mane that don't invest in bulk with Raging Bull.

EV Spreads
  • 244 HP / 12 Atk / 76 Def / 36 SpD / 140 Spe with Adamant: This EV spread allows Paldean Tauros-B to defeat Flutter Mane with Trailblaze into Raging Bull. The Defense EVs allow it to beat Choice Band Chien-Pao after Intimidate one-on-one. The Speed investment allows Paldean Tauros-B to outpace Flutter Mane after Trailblaze.

strategies.overview:
Draft Order: Round 7 onward

Price Range: 5-6 points

Overview: Paldean Tauros-F works as a decent defensive answer to some physically offensive foes. It sets itself apart from other cheap Fighting-type options with a solid secondary typing, burn immunity, defensive options in Will-O-Wisp and Intimidate, and serviceable Defense and Attack with a unique STAB option in Raging Bull to remove dual screens. Unfortunately, its stronger STAB options in Flare Blitz and Close Combat come with drawbacks such as recoil and lowered defensive stats, contradicting its defensive traits and utility. Body Press and Raging Bull can make up for this somewhat, but they often lack enough power to be threatening consistently. Without pivoting, reliable recovery, and good stats outside of Attack and Defense, Paldean Tauros-F struggles to provide much value in most games.
strategies.comments:
Common Roles

Bulky Wall: Paldean Tauros-F can utilize Intimidate and its natural typing to take hits and punish with an attack or Will-O-Wisp. However, it struggles long-term due to Flare Blitz recoil, chip damage from entry hazards and contact effects, and its lack of reliable healing options.

Wallbreaker: Paldean Tauros-F can equip a damage-boosting item and use its STAB moves and coverage to wallbreak for its teammates, but its average base Speed allows it to easily get revenge killed or taken advantage of.

Late-game Cleaner: Paldean Tauros-F can clean up weakened teams using its setup option in Bulk Up and Speed-boosting options in Trailblaze and Flame Charge. Alternatively, it can use Choice Scarf for instant Speed.

Common Moves

Primary STAB Moves: Raging Bull, Flare Blitz, Body Press, Close Combat

Setup Moves: Bulk Up, Trailblaze, Flame Charge

Utility Moves: Will-O-Wisp

Coverage: Earthquake, Lash Out, Iron Head, Rock Slide, Stone Edge, Wild Charge, Zen Headbutt

Niche Moves

Endure: Endure alongside Rocky Helmet can accrue additional chip damage on physical attackers, even when Paldean Tauros-F is in range of a KO.

Endeavor: Paldean Tauros-F can utilize its Speed to leave targets in KO range for a teammate if it cannot muscle past them naturally.

Rock Tomb/ Bulldoze: Paldean Tauros-F can use Rock Tomb or Bulldoze to lower the opposing Pokemon's Speed and outpace and KO a faster threat.

Rest / Sleep Talk: Rest can be used alongside a Chesto Berry or Sleep Talk to grant immediate recovery in a pinch. This can allow Paldean Tauros-F to be a more reliable long-term check to specific offensive wallbreakers.

Common Items

Rocky Helmet: Paldean Tauros-F can punish prominent physical attackers and U-turn users with Rocky Helmet.

Damage-boosting Items: Paldean Tauros-F can use relevant damage-boosting items such as Choice Band, Life Orb, Expert Belt, and Charcoal to assist in its wallbreaking potential.

Heavy-Duty Boots: Heavy-Duty Boots allows Paldean Tauros-F to be immune to entry hazard chip damage over time, increasing its longevity.

Choice Scarf: Paldean Tauros-F can hold a Choice Scarf to act as a revenge killer and outpace threats that would otherwise outspeed it naturally.

Niche Items

Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry can boost Paldean Tauros-F's longevity and be used alongside Cud Chew to increase its recovery at the cost of giving up Intimidate.

Assault Vest: An Assault Vest can shore up Paldean Tauros-F's meager Special Defense to take some hits from prominent special attackers.

Leftovers: Leftovers grants Paldean Tauros-F recovery over time, assuming it is on the field long enough to get enough value over other items.

Chesto Berry: A Chesto Berry can allow Paldean Tauros-F to immediately wake up after using Rest.

Tera

Paldean Tauros-F doesn't need to be a Tera Captain to be successful in its roles, as its serviceable base typing is often enough to get the job done. However, if Paldean Tauros-F is a Tera Captain, it can utilize both Tera Fire and Fighting to boost its STAB moves and increase its wallbreaking potential. Paldean Tauros-F can also use other types such as Tera Water, Fairy, Grass, and Dragon to provide more defensive utility and grant access to new or improved coverage options with Tera Blast.

Draft Strategy

Paldean Tauros-F should be drafted as a check to physical Grass-, Steel-, Fire-, and Dark-type Pokemon such as Meowscarada, Gouging Fire, and Roaring Moon, though it is often outclassed by cheaper picks that can provide more utility and role compression to a team.

Pivots: Pokemon such as Tornadus-T and Galarian Slowking can take a hit and allow Paldean Tauros-F safe entry.

Entry Hazard Control: Paldean Tauros-F appreciates Pokemon that can reliably set entry hazards, such as Deoxys-S and Great Tusk, as well as hazard removers such as Iron Treads and Great Tusk to keep it healthy.

Checks and Counters

Bulky Resistant Foes: Pokemon that can stomach a hit from Paldean Tauros-F, especially those who do not fear Will-O-Wisp, such as Pecharunt and Latias, can deal with it and fire back with status or a strong attack.

Chip Damage: Pokemon such as Garchomp and Zapdos can chip at Paldean Tauros-F when holding a Rocky Helmet, stacking up alongside potential Flare Blitz recoil and entry hazard damage.

Faster Pokemon: Pokemon such as Greninja, Keldeo, and Iron Bundle can all outpace Paldean Tauros-F and KO with a super effective attack.

Special Attackers: Paldean Tauros-F's poor Special Defense leaves it susceptible to strong special attackers, such as Zapdos, Kyurem, and Iron Valiant.
